H6MO05254.name: Jordan Herrera
H6MO05254.bio: Air Force veteran, attorney, and former Assistant Attorney General.

positions.stance: Believes "every American should be able to afford housing, healthcare, quality education, and food security while working one job."
Supports the nation's military and veterans and pledges to "never leave them behind," while saying "we cannot waste taxpayer dollars."
"The federal government should not be able to regulate your body, your marriage, your religion in schools, or your personal life decisions."
Supports expanding affordable housing in rural and urban communities, rebuilding local healthcare access, reinvesting in rural hospitals and schools, and modernizing infrastructure.
Commits to securing federal funding for local projects, supporting small businesses and agriculture, modernizing transportation, and improving public safety in Missouri's 4th District.

H4MO05234.name: Emanuel Cleaver
H4MO05234.bio: U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth District, serving his eleventh term; former Kansas City council member and mayor.

positions.stance: Calls accessible, affordable housing for all "a life-long crusade" and cites bipartisan work on a major housing reform law.
Will keep fighting for investments to keep Social Security and Medicare solvent, and supports expanding Medicaid and closing coverage gaps for rural and underserved communities.
Supports and defends the Affordable Care Act, believes it "should be strengthened," and seeks to lower prescription drug costs.
Disagrees with overturning Roe v. Wade and believes "reproductive health care decisions need to be between women and their doctors."
Supports "bipartisan, common-sense gun safety legislation" while respecting responsible gun ownership, and funding, resources and training for law enforcement.

H2MO04199.name: Rick Brattin
H2MO04199.bio: Marine Corps veteran and small business owner; Missouri state senator and chair of the Senate Education Committee, former state representative and Cass County Auditor.

positions.stance: Says he will be "a strong ally for the administration" in advancing President Trump's goal to Make America Great Again.
Pledges to "stand firm against any attempt to infringe on our God-given right to keep and bear arms."
Describes himself as "100% pro-life" and says he will fight to defund Planned Parenthood.
Will back efforts to build the wall, fully fund ICE, deport criminal illegal aliens, and end policies that encouraged illegal immigration.
Supports cutting taxes, slashing regulations and unleashing American energy, and will fight reckless spending that drives up the national debt and inflation.

H6MO06260.name: Josh Smead
H6MO06260.bio: Licensed architect, small business owner, and project professional from Liberty, Missouri.

positions.stance: Supports smart trade, farmers' right to repair equipment, expanded market access, and "policies that prioritize family farms so rural communities can thrive."
Wants to stop the administration from holding up 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding, diversify the electrical grid, and support the Grain Belt Express project.
Supports fully funding broadband expansion, especially in rural areas, regulating major telecom companies, and investigating the costs versus benefits of data centers to residents.
"I support moving America to a universal healthcare system," with funding for rural access and struggling hospitals and lower prescription prices.
Opposes school vouchers and federal money for private religious schools; supports more public school funding, universal school meals and universal pre-K.

H6MO06310.name: Chris Stigall
H6MO06310.bio: Nationally syndicated conservative talk radio host and former field representative and deputy communications director for Congressman Sam Graves.

positions.stance: "The Second Amendment is not negotiable"; will oppose federal efforts to restrict the rights of law-abiding gun owners.
Will work to reduce red tape, expand access to care, and strengthen rural hospitals so small-town families can get quality healthcare close to home.
Describes himself as "proudly pro-life" and will oppose taxpayer funding for abortion.
Supports making President Trump's tax cuts permanent and will fight any effort to raise taxes on hardworking Americans.
Supports expanding market access and reducing regulations on family farms, and will seek a seat on the House Agriculture Committee.
"Cut wasteful government spending and let hardworking Missourians keep more of what they earn."
"Make healthcare affordable and put patients — not bureaucrats — back in charge of their care."
"Secure our southern border and defend the constitutional rights of every law-abiding American."
"Drain the swamp of waste, fraud, and abuse — and answer to the people, not the political class."
Supports closing tax loopholes "to End Billionaire Welfare," protecting Social Security, paid family and medical leave, and banning grocery price gouging and junk fees.
Supports investing in rural education and workforce training, ending gerrymandering, children's data privacy, and raising teacher pay.
Supports "Medicare for all who want it," veterans' healthcare access, rural hospital stabilization, and Medicare drug price negotiation.
Supports right-to-repair, protecting U.S. farmland from foreign adversaries, and crop insurance reform, and opposes AI data centers.
Supports releasing the Epstein files, banning congressional stock trading, auditing the Pentagon, ending Citizens United, and congressional term limits.

H4MO08162.name: Jason Smith
H4MO08162.bio: U.S. Representative for Missouri's 8th congressional district and member of the House Ways and Means Committee; former Missouri House Speaker Pro Tem, farmer and small business owner.

H6MO08183.name: Christopher Reichard
H6MO08183.bio: Disabled Army veteran of Operation Iraqi Freedom and second-generation IBEW Local 1 union member from Arnold, Missouri.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare-For-All and stepping-stone bills toward it, breaking up medical monopolies, and funding rural hospitals and clinics.
Supports ending private education voucher systems that take resources from public education, and fair wages and incentives to retain educators.
Backs pro-labor bills like the PRO Act and calls for "fair trade that protects American workers, small businesses and farmers."
Supports restoring checks and balances, defunding and abolishing ICE, ending Citizens United, a Supreme Court ethics code, and congressional term limits and stock-trading bans.
"Our veterans served for us, and now their benefits are under attack."

H8WI01156.name: Bryan Steil
H8WI01156.bio: U.S. Representative serving Southeast Wisconsin in Congress.

positions.stance: Leading efforts "to cut wasteful spending and lower costs for Wisconsin workers and families."
"We must secure our border"; supports policies to stop the flow of illicit fentanyl and end human trafficking, and working with law enforcement.
Committed to protecting Social Security and Medicare and keeping them solvent, and working to lower prescription drug prices.
Working to support service members, their families and veterans, including mental health access and earned benefits; "proudly supports the Second Amendment."
Supports policies to lower costs for families; "He supports access to IVF and is a strong supporter of life."

H6WI01283.name: Mitchell Berman
H6WI01283.bio: Registered nurse with more than 23 years in health care, including over a decade at the VA, and a board-certified emergency nurse.

positions.stance: Supports raising the federal minimum wage, cracking down on grocery price gouging and rent-price fixing, lowering child care costs, and expanding the child tax credit.
Supports restoring ACA subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, creating a public option, and capping out-of-pocket prescription costs including $35 insulin for everyone.
Supports overturning Citizens United, ending dark money, banning stock trading by members of Congress, the president and vice president, and Supreme Court ethics rules.
Supports passing the PRO Act, prioritizing companies that hire locally for federal contracts and incentives, and expanding apprenticeships and skilled trades.
Says Congress must uphold its duty to decide when to declare war, and "We should end the costly, reckless war in Iran."

H2WI02124.name: Mark Pocan
H2WI02124.bio: U.S. Representative since 2013, former Wisconsin State Assembly member and Dane County supervisor, and longtime owner of a union printing business.

positions.stance: Supports strengthening unemployment compensation, higher education assistance, worker rights and pension protections, health care for the vulnerable, and Medicare and Social Security.
Believes "we must embrace the challenge of ensuring that illness, job loss, old age or disability does not mean a life sentence of poverty."

H0WI03175.name: Derrick Van Orden
H0WI03175.bio: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's Third Congressional District and retired Navy SEAL Senior Chief after 26 years in the Navy; former small business owner.

positions.stance: Committed to ensuring western Wisconsin has "safe, clean drinking water, well-maintained roads and bridges, and reliable rural broadband."
Champions legislation like the Working Family Tax Cuts so more hard-earned money stays in Wisconsinites' pockets.
Says he is working "for every person in his district, regardless of political party, not for the political leaders in D.C."
Will work to protect people with preexisting conditions when Obamacare is fully repealed and replaced by a system allowing true competition to drive costs down.
Works to cut red tape at the VA, make physical and mental health treatment more accessible, and create education, employment and housing pathways for veterans.

H4WI03169.name: Rebecca Cooke
H4WI03169.bio: Former owner of Red's Mercantile, founder of the Red Letter Grant nonprofit for women entrepreneurs, Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation board member, and restaurant server.

positions.stance: Supports a $30/month cap on essential drugs, expanding Medicare to vision, dental and hearing, reversing Medicaid and ACA cuts, and ending "the costly Iran War."
Supports banning stock trading for Congress and the White House, ending Citizens United, congressional term limits, and fully funding law enforcement and border protection.
Supports expanding export markets, enforcing antitrust laws against Big Ag, protecting farmland from foreign buyers, and ending tariffs that cut off agricultural marketplaces.
Supports cutting permitting and licensing red tape, expanding small-business tax deductions and credits, and incentives for using Made in America inputs.
Supports a $15/hour federal minimum wage, new green infrastructure, passing the PRO Act, and tax credits for first-time home buyers.

H4WI04183.name: Gwen Moore
H4WI04183.bio: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District since 2005 and member of the Ways and Means Committee; former Wisconsin state senator and assembly member.

positions.stance: Advocates for improving economic and employment conditions in low-income communities, curbing predatory lending, helping small businesses grow, and more affordable housing.
Supports ensuring low-income students have school access to three nutritious meals a day year-round, and advocates for Federal TRIO college-access programs.
Advocates for ensuring service members and veterans get PTSD care, confidential military mental health services, and increased PTSD research and treatment funding.

H4WI04274.name: Tim Rogers
H4WI04274.bio: Milwaukee resident who has worked for almost 30 years delivering gift baskets and newspapers for two local businesses.

positions.stance: "I support School Choice and School Voucher programs," calling them the best option in many urban districts for students to reach their full potential.
Supports harsh punishment for violent criminals, and believes rights should be "immediately and fully restored" once a citizen has served their sentence.
Would make declaring "a clean water emergency" for areas most in need a first priority and replace pipes that risk children's health.
Wants less government spending, to let taxpayers keep more of their money, to "destroy the progressive tax system," and to shrink agencies through attrition.

H0WI05113.name: Scott Fitzgerald
H0WI05113.bio: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's Fifth Congressional District since 2020; former Wisconsin state senator, newspaper publisher, and 27-year Army Reserve officer.

positions.stance: "In Congress, Scott Fitzgerald will take the fight to the radical liberals pushing socialism."
Will "continue to work in Congress to grow our economy and help small businesses thrive again."
Will work with President Trump "to stop the illegal drug trade, end illegal immigration, and put America's national security first."
Describes himself as "a proud and loyal supporter of all those who sacrifice to keep us safe."
"He'll fight to defend our country and honor those who served."

H6WI05136.name: Andrew Beck
H6WI05136.bio: Built a career in healthcare and business, working alongside Wisconsin workers and manufacturers.

positions.stance: Will fight to "Stop Trump's radical agenda & safeguard our Democracy," saying "Protecting democracy protects every other right we have."
Will fight to defend women's healthcare rights and secure protections in Congress: "No rights should be decided by politicians."
Will fight to protect the promise of Social Security: "Retirement dignity begins with protecting Social Security."
Will fight to protect and strengthen Medicare, saying "Medicare and Medicaid are lifelines that must be protected."
Will fight to help farmers with government backing: "Wisconsin farmers deserve a fair shot for a strong future."

H4WI06048.name: Glenn Grothman
H4WI06048.bio: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 6th congressional district since 2014; former Wisconsin State Assembly member and State Senate assistant majority leader, and former estate-planning attorney and tax preparer.

positions.stance: "Promote skills-based education."
"Keep open work centers for those with disabilities."
"Get rid of the marriage penalty for government assistance programs."
"Refinance student loans."
"Get more generic medication on the market."
"Raise minimum wage, expand apprenticeships, and reward companies that create and expand jobs right here at home."
Supports affordable healthcare "as a Right": lower costs, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, and keep care close to home.
"Increase access to tech schools, college, trades, apprenticeships, and lifelong learning so every worker can thrive."
Supports requiring "transparency, strong safeguards, and accountability for massive data center developments before they move forward."
"Restore prevailing wage, strengthen Project Labor Agreements, and protect the right to organize."

H6WI07223.name: Michael Alfonso
H6WI07223.bio: Former construction and concrete worker and former producer of The Dan Bongino Show podcast.

positions.stance: Will "rein in spending, cut red tape, and make it possible for young families to own homes again."
Will cut burdensome restrictions, support local agriculture, and make healthy food affordable to fight chronic illness and prevent childhood obesity.
Will support school choice, boost homeschooling protections, and "end Marxist race and gender indoctrination in classrooms."
Describes himself as "100% Pro Life," opposes expanding mail-in abortion pills, and rejects efforts to expand assisted suicide.
Will "put America First, fix problems here, and stop wasteful foreign spending."

H6WI07207.name: Fred Clark
H6WI07207.bio: Forester and land manager and former rural Wisconsin legislator.

positions.stance: Says realizing the benefits of AI technology requires "a strong public oversight of this technology and how it is built out."
Says AI has tremendous potential, "But without adequate guardrails, AI also creates huge new risks for all of us."
"I firmly support the freedom for women to make choices about reproductive care with their doctors," including access to contraception.
Supports a secure border and prosecuting and deporting criminals, while guaranteeing "the rights of law-abiding people who are in this country legally."
Says leaders must do their part to uphold the Constitution and that "Today the guarantees of our constitution for Americans are at risk."

H4WI08119.name: Tony Wied
H4WI08119.bio: Businessman who spent three decades starting, building, and operating businesses in Northeast Wisconsin, including Dino Stop gas stations.

positions.stance: Prioritized finishing the border wall, reinstituting the Remain in Mexico policy, and ensuring border agents have needed funding.
Says "The national debt is out of control" and that Washington needs small-business-style leadership to balance the books.
Will work with President Trump to pass his America First agenda, secure the border, support the military, and protect Wisconsin values.
Will "fight to keep our military strong and eliminate any threat of terrorism inside of our borders."
Will "work to reduce government regulations to unleash America's energy potential."

H6WI08205.name: Rick Crosson
H6WI08205.bio: U.S. Army veteran who has served in business and on the school board.

positions.stance: "No one is above the law, including the president, the wealthy, and the powerful. Congress must do the oversight it has walked away from."
Supports lower costs for groceries, gas, housing, child care and health care, and "A fair and living wage no one should fall below."
"No data centers without strict state and federal regulation," with prepayment so taxpayers don't bear costs and local communities determining the outcome.
Supports "Affordable, Accessible, Guaranteed Healthcare for Everyone," price transparency, lower prescription costs, and freedom to choose your doctor.
Supports passing "critical immigration reform with a focus on laws that reward hard work and contribution."
Calls healthcare a human right and says "It's time we pass Medicare for All."
Calls for ending all wars and an arms embargo, opposing U.S. tax dollars funding what she calls "a genocide in Palestine."
"We must Abolish ICE," replacing it with "a humane, accountable immigration system focused on genuine public safety."
Supports universal childcare and eldercare so "every child has a safe place to grow and everyone has freedom to plan their future."
Urges "NO on 87 No tax increase," no on NN in support of TABOR, and yes on measures 133, 134 and 135.
"Low tax, limited Gov, Peace through Strength."
"Safe Cities ~ Strong Economy ~ Safe Schools."
"Review all SS finances to reach solvency, cut debt."
Calls Denver's homeless population problem "not safe nor acceptable" and says "Let's get people off the streets."

H8CO02160.name: Joe Neguse
H8CO02160.bio: U.S. Representative for Colorado's 2nd District and former chair of the House Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests and Public Lands.

positions.stance: Committed to preserving Colorado's public spaces, investing in the outdoor recreation economy, safeguarding wildlife and biodiversity, and tackling western wildfires.
Believes climate change is "an existential threat" requiring bold action, including renewable energy investment and drastically reduced carbon emissions.
Supports universal health care coverage, lowering prescription drug costs, expanding Medicare, and combating discriminatory practices of for-profit insurers.
Fighting to close the gender pay gap and raise the minimum wage to $15, and advocating for paid leave, affordable child care and expanded nutrition assistance.
Supports the Equality Act for LGBTQ+ Americans, the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, and the EACH Woman Act on women's healthcare decisions.

H6CO02206.name: Kelley Dennison
H6CO02206.bio: Colorado native from Estes Park, business owner, and activist.

positions.stance: Supports reducing federal spending that fuels inflation, lowering energy costs through domestic production, making homeownership achievable, and protecting small businesses.
Believes "conservation and economic prosperity can coexist"; supports watershed protection, wildfire mitigation, and responsible energy development with local input.
Supports policies that help families thrive and believes "CO-02 must do better by our veterans and senior citizens."
Says every child deserves a safe, high-quality education, and parents "should be informed and empowered partners in their children's education."
Calls the Second Amendment a constitutional right and says "Responsible gun owners should not be punished for the actions of criminals."
"We must secure the border immediately"; strongly supports legal immigration and giving Border Patrol and law enforcement all necessary resources.
Prioritizes higher-paying jobs in rural Colorado, targeting unnecessary mandates and regulations and helping small businesses start, grow, and succeed.
Will explore savings for rural families, including the Child Tax Credit and tax credits and investments that assist parents with child care.
Supports responsible development of all Colorado energy resources, is open to competitively priced renewables, and backs permitting and regulatory reform.
Will push lower Colorado River Basin users "to live within their water means" and seek permitting changes for critical Colorado water projects.

H6CO03253.name: Dwayne Romero
H6CO03253.bio: Army combat veteran and small business owner; former school board president, city councilman, and Colorado Director of Economic Development.

positions.stance: Calls affordability his top priority and will fight to make ends meet easier, "starting with repealing these disastrous tariffs and expanding the Family Tax Credits."
"We must pass a robust Farm Bill and keep foreign entities out of Colorado water and farmland ownership."
Says Congress needs someone "who will hold the line for our district's water resources," calling this "job number one."
Supports an all-of-the-above approach, using local legacy energy resources while pressing hard on advancing and deploying alternative energies.
Opposes efforts to sell or transfer public lands to private interests, and supports firefighters and increased fire resilience.
